ap_macroeconomics-m14.stem: An economy is at its natural rate of unemployment with stable inflation. The central bank increases the growth rate of the money supply to stimulate the economy. In the short run, the economy moves along its short-run Phillips curve. In the long run, workers and firms fully adjust their inflation expectations. Which of the following describes the short-run and long-run effects compared with the initial situation?

options.text: In the short run, unemployment is lower and inflation is higher; in the long run, unemployment is higher and inflation is higher.

Once expectations adjust, the short-run Phillips curve shifts and unemployment returns to the natural rate on the vertical long-run Phillips curve. Expected inflation has caught up, so inflation stays higher than in the initial situation.

options.text: In the short run, unemployment is lower and inflation is unchanged; in the long run, unemployment is unchanged and inflation is higher.
options.why: Says the short-run inflation rate would not change, but it would increase. Along the short-run Phillips curve, lower unemployment goes with higher inflation.

options.text: In the short run, unemployment is lower and inflation is lower; in the long run, unemployment is unchanged and inflation is higher.
options.why: Says the short-run inflation rate would decrease, but it would increase. Along the short-run Phillips curve, lower unemployment goes with higher inflation.

options.text: In the short run, unemployment is lower and inflation is higher; in the long run, unemployment is unchanged and inflation is unchanged.
options.why: Says the long-run inflation rate would not change, but it would increase. Expected inflation has caught up, so inflation stays higher than in the initial situation.
